headline: ICE detains fifth Cumberland County corrections officer in under two years
dek: Maine Public reports that Dannick Massamba-Bankela was detained during a scheduled appointment in Scarborough; his lawyer says he has a pending asylum claim and no criminal record.
body: Immigration and Customs Enforcement detained another Cumberland County Jail corrections officer Tuesday, the fifth officer detained in less than two years, according to Maine Public. The officer was identified as Dannick Massamba-Bankela.

Massamba-Bankela arrived at ICE’s Scarborough field office with his lawyer for a scheduled appointment after supporters learned he had been told to return to the office. Volunteers gathered outside to help his family and connect them with legal and financial support, Maine Public reported.

His lawyer said Massamba-Bankela is originally from the Republic of the Congo, entered the United States on a visa, has a pending asylum claim and has work authorization. She also said he has no criminal record. Those details were provided by his lawyer and were not independently verified in the report.

The lawyer said ICE agents told her Massamba-Bankela was being detained for overstaying a visa. An ICE spokesperson did not immediately respond to Maine Public’s request for comment. The detention adds to a series of cases involving Cumberland County corrections staff as immigration enforcement expands in Maine.
author: NorthEast News Desk
